page.overview:
Who is Christabel Udolpho?

Christabel Udolpho is a member of the House of Udolpho, a Tilean house with an estate of the same name in the Principality of Miragliano.

Christabel is Guido Ravaglioli and Flaminea Udolpho's daughter. Christabel is an emotional, flamboyant young Udolpho, obsessed with playing the harpsichord. She is a known weirdroot addict. She believes herself to be a master seductress. She was educated in the Empire, at the academy in Nuln, and recently returned to Udolpho, scandalising her mother with the habits she appeared to have acquired during her time away from the family estate. Once, after a dispute about the ownership of a bonnet, Christabel had ominously told her mother that she had taken a course under Valancourt of Nuln, the master swordsman, and would be only too pleased to give a demonstration of her carving skills.

Christabel had learned music in Nuln and possessed a pleasant although not outstanding voice. She likes to say that she was often praised by the Elector Countess Emmanuelle von Liebwitz of Nuln. At the academy, she had also begun to get the measure of her own charms and is clearly more than a little frustrated to have left the high society of the Empire to return to Udolpho, where her opportunities for breaking hearts are now severely limited. Since she drove Praz the gamekeeper to suicide, there has been no one to torment with her sable-black hair, liquid eyes and silky skin. She spent much of her time wandering the broken battlements of Udolpho, fretting and plotting, shroud-like dresses flapping in the breeze, petting the ravens.

She schemes to first expel her relatives from Udolpho and cut them loose in the outside world. She believes that none of them would last a month. Then, she'd dismantle the house, stone by stone, until she had the Black Cygnet's treasure. Then, as the wealthiest woman of the Known World, she would return to the great cities of the Empire, of Bretonnia, and Kislev, and make all men her slaves. She believed entire countries were hers for the taking.
